# Purpose and inputs

This document contains the statistical analysis for the manuscript *Perceived
Stress and Vaginal Lactobacillus Species Among Patients With Ovarian Cancer in
the ORCHiD Study*, including all tables, figures, and Supplementary Table S1.

**Scope.** The analysis starts from **prepared analysis datasets**. It does not
process sequencing data and does not derive the microbiome measures. The
following are produced upstream and are read here as columns:

- 16S rRNA processing (DADA2, SILVA taxonomy), species assignment, and relative
  abundances;
- Shannon diversity (ASV level);
- the *Lactobacillus* dominance indicator (genus relative abundance ≥ 50%);
- the species detection indicators (species-assigned relative abundance > 0) and
  *L. iners* relative abundance;
- the latent Dirichlet allocation topic model from the parent ORCHiD analysis;
- the PSS-4 total score and registry-derived stage and histologic subtype
  categories.

**What this file does.** It reads the prepared files, standardizes PSS-4 to a
z-score, builds the analysis factors and binary outcome variables, identifies the
*Lactobacillus*-dominated topic, fits every model reported in the manuscript,
generates Tables 1–3, Supplementary Table S1 and Figures 1–2, and writes them to
disk so no reported value is copied by hand.

**Required input files** (placed in `params$data_dir`; set the parameter when
knitting, e.g. `rmarkdown::render("ORCHiD_PSS4_Lactobacillus_Analysis.Rmd",
params = list(data_dir = "path/to/data"))`):

| File | Prepared columns used |
|---|---|
| `complete_stress_dysbiosis_dataset.csv` | One row per analytic participant: `SampleID`; `pss4_sum` (PSS-4 total, 0–16); `age` (or `age.x`); `race_clean` (`NH-White`/`NH-Black`); `stage_clean` (`Early`/`Late`); `hist_clean` (`Type I + Other`/`Type II`); `shannon_diversity` (ASV-level Shannon index); `lactobacillus_dominance` (indicator, genus relative abundance ≥ 50%) |
| `final_species_enhanced_dataset.csv` | `SampleID`; `crispatus_detected`, `iners_detected`, `gasseri_detected`, `jensenii_detected` (indicators, species-assigned relative abundance > 0); `iners_abundance` (*L. iners* relative abundance, 0–1) |
| `topic_model_results.rds` | Output of the latent Dirichlet allocation fit in the parent ORCHiD analysis; list element `gamma` with columns `document` (= `SampleID`), `topic`, `gamma` |

**Where each manuscript item is produced**

| Manuscript item | Section |
|---|---|
| Table 1 | [Table 1](#table1) |
| Table 2, Figure 1 | [Species detection](#species), [Community and genus measures](#comparators), [Table 2 and Figure 1](#table2) |
| Table 3, Figure 2 | [Race interaction and stratified models](#race) |
| Supplementary Table S1 | [Sensitivity analyses](#sensitivity) |

## Analysis plan

**Exposure.** PSS-4 total score standardized to mean 0, SD 1 (`pss4_z`) in the
analytic sample and modeled continuously. Every estimate is per 1-SD increase in
PSS-4 (3.43 points).

**Outcomes.**

| Role | Outcome | Model | Adjustment |
|---|---|---|---|
| Species (one correction family) | Detection of *L. crispatus*, *L. iners*, *L. gasseri*, *L. jensenii* (supplied indicators; species-assigned relative abundance > 0) | Firth logistic | race, age |
| Community / genus | Shannon diversity | Linear regression | race, age, stage, histologic subtype |
| | *Lactobacillus* dominance (supplied indicator; genus relative abundance ≥ 50%) | Firth logistic | race, age, stage, histologic subtype |
| | *Lactobacillus*-dominated topic membership | Beta regression, logit link | race, age, stage, histologic subtype |
| Race | Shannon diversity, *Lactobacillus* dominance | Interaction model (`pss4_z * race + age`) and age-adjusted models within each racial group | age |

**Multiple testing.** Benjamini–Hochberg false discovery rate correction is
applied across the four species-detection tests only (q < 0.05). Community,
genus, race, and sensitivity analyses are reported with unadjusted P values.

# Packages

```{r packages}
required_packages <- c("tidyverse", "broom", "logistf", "betareg", "splines", "patchwork")

missing_packages <- required_packages[
  !vapply(required_packages, requireNamespace, logical(1), quietly = TRUE)
]
if (length(missing_packages) > 0) {
  stop("Install before knitting: ", paste(missing_packages, collapse = ", "))
}

library(tidyverse)
library(broom)
library(logistf)    # Firth penalized logistic regression
library(betareg)    # beta regression for topic membership
library(splines)    # natural cubic spline for the linearity check
library(patchwork)  # combines figure panels

set.seed(243)

cat(R.version.string, "\n")
cat("logistf", as.character(packageVersion("logistf")),
    "| betareg", as.character(packageVersion("betareg")), "\n")
```

# Data

```{r load}
data_dir <- params$data_dir

read_input <- function(filename) {
  path <- file.path(data_dir, filename)
  if (!file.exists(path)) stop("Input file not found: ", path)
  path
}

standardize_age_name <- function(df) {
  if ("age"   %in% names(df)) return(df)
  if ("age.x" %in% names(df)) return(dplyr::rename(df, age = age.x))
  stop("No age or age.x column found.")
}

to_binary <- function(x, positive = c("yes", "true", "1")) {
  if (is.logical(x)) return(as.integer(x))
  if (is.numeric(x)) return(as.integer(x > 0))
  as.integer(stringr::str_to_lower(stringr::str_trim(as.character(x))) %in% positive)
}

stress_raw  <- readr::read_csv(read_input("complete_stress_dysbiosis_dataset.csv"),
                               show_col_types = FALSE) |> standardize_age_name()
species_raw <- readr::read_csv(read_input("final_species_enhanced_dataset.csv"),
                               show_col_types = FALSE)

for (nm in c("stress_raw", "species_raw")) {
  if (anyDuplicated(get(nm)$SampleID)) stop("Duplicate SampleID in ", nm)
}
```

```{r species-columns}
species_map <- c(
  "L. crispatus" = "crispatus_detected",
  "L. iners"     = "iners_detected",
  "L. gasseri"   = "gasseri_detected",
  "L. jensenii"  = "jensenii_detected"
)

missing_cols <- setdiff(c(unname(species_map), "iners_abundance"), names(species_raw))
if (length(missing_cols) > 0) {
  stop("Species columns not found: ", paste(missing_cols, collapse = ", "),
       "\nEdit `species_map` to match names(species_raw).")
}
```

```{r analytic-data}
dat <- stress_raw |>
  mutate(
    pss4_z = as.numeric(scale(pss4_sum)),
    race   = factor(race_clean,  levels = c("NH-White", "NH-Black")),
    stage  = factor(stage_clean, levels = c("Early", "Late")),
    hist   = factor(hist_clean,  levels = c("Type I + Other", "Type II")),
    lactobacillus_dominance = to_binary(lactobacillus_dominance)
  )

species_outcomes <- species_raw |>
  transmute(
    SampleID,
    crispatus_detected = to_binary(.data[[species_map[["L. crispatus"]]]]),
    iners_detected     = to_binary(.data[[species_map[["L. iners"]]]]),
    gasseri_detected   = to_binary(.data[[species_map[["L. gasseri"]]]]),
    jensenii_detected  = to_binary(.data[[species_map[["L. jensenii"]]]]),
    iners_abundance    = as.numeric(iners_abundance)
  )

# PSS-4 is standardized once, in `dat`, and carried into `spec` by SampleID so
# that every model uses the same z-score.
spec <- dat |>
  select(SampleID, pss4_sum, pss4_z, race, age, stage, hist) |>
  inner_join(species_outcomes, by = "SampleID")

species_vars <- c("crispatus_detected", "iners_detected",
                  "gasseri_detected",   "jensenii_detected")

species_labels <- c(
  crispatus_detected = "L. crispatus detection",
  iners_detected     = "L. iners detection",
  gasseri_detected   = "L. gasseri detection",
  jensenii_detected  = "L. jensenii detection"
)

stopifnot(all(c("shannon_diversity", "lactobacillus_dominance") %in% names(dat)))
stopifnot(nrow(spec) == nrow(dat))
if (nrow(dat) != 123) warning("Analytic sample has ", nrow(dat),
                              " rows; the manuscript analytic sample is 123.")

cat("Analytic N:", nrow(dat), "\n")
cat("PSS-4 mean (SD):", round(mean(dat$pss4_sum), 2),
    "(", round(sd(dat$pss4_sum), 2), ") | 1-SD =", round(sd(dat$pss4_sum), 2), "points\n")
```

## Event counts

Event counts determine which adjustment set each outcome can support and make
sparse or empty cells visible before modeling.

```{r event-counts}
analysis_counts <- bind_rows(
  tibble(outcome = "Shannon diversity",
         analytic_n = sum(complete.cases(dat[c("shannon_diversity", "pss4_z",
                                               "race", "age", "stage", "hist")])),
         events = NA_integer_),
  tibble(outcome = "Lactobacillus dominance (>=50%)",
         analytic_n = nrow(dat),
         events = sum(dat$lactobacillus_dominance == 1, na.rm = TRUE)),
  map_dfr(species_vars, \(v) tibble(
    outcome    = unname(species_labels[v]),
    analytic_n = nrow(spec),
    events     = sum(spec[[v]] == 1, na.rm = TRUE)
  ))
)
analysis_counts

for (v in species_vars) {
  cat("\n", unname(species_labels[v]), " by race:\n", sep = "")
  print(table(Race = spec$race, Detected = spec[[v]]))
}
```

*L. crispatus* is detected only among NH-White participants (a zero cell), which
is one reason Firth penalized regression is used: ordinary logistic regression
cannot return a finite estimate under separation.

# Helper functions

These extract one term from a fitted model into a table-ready row. The `.env`
and `.data` pronouns are deliberate: `broom::tidy()` returns a numeric column
named `statistic`, which `dplyr` can otherwise confuse with the label argument.

```{r helpers}
extract_lm_term <- function(model, term, outcome, adjustment, statistic = "Beta") {
  broom::tidy(model, conf.int = TRUE) |>
    filter(.data$term == .env$term) |>
    transmute(outcome = .env$outcome, statistic = .env$statistic,
              estimate = .data$estimate, conf_low = .data$conf.low,
              conf_high = .data$conf.high, p_value = .data$p.value,
              adjustment = .env$adjustment)
}

# Firth models: profile penalized-likelihood confidence intervals and
# penalized likelihood-ratio P values (the logistf defaults).
extract_firth_term <- function(model, term, outcome, adjustment, statistic = "OR") {
  index <- match(term, names(coef(model)))
  if (is.na(index)) stop("Term not found in Firth model: ", term)
  tibble(outcome = as.character(outcome), statistic = as.character(statistic),
         estimate  = as.numeric(exp(coef(model)[index])),
         conf_low  = as.numeric(exp(model$ci.lower[index])),
         conf_high = as.numeric(exp(model$ci.upper[index])),
         p_value   = as.numeric(model$prob[index]),
         adjustment = as.character(adjustment))
}

format_result <- function(estimate, conf_low, conf_high, digits = 2) {
  paste0(formatC(estimate,  format = "f", digits = digits), " (",
         formatC(conf_low,  format = "f", digits = digits), ", ",
         formatC(conf_high, format = "f", digits = digits), ")")
}
```

# Table 1 — participant characteristics {#table1}

Two-sample t tests for continuous variables and Fisher exact tests for
categorical variables, comparing NH-White and NH-Black participants.

```{r table1}
t1_continuous <- function(d, var, label) {
  tt <- stats::t.test(stats::as.formula(paste(var, "~ race")), data = d)
  ms <- function(x) sprintf("%.1f (%.1f)", mean(x, na.rm = TRUE), sd(x, na.rm = TRUE))
  tibble(characteristic = label,
         overall  = ms(d[[var]]),
         nh_white = ms(d[[var]][d$race == "NH-White"]),
         nh_black = ms(d[[var]][d$race == "NH-Black"]),
         p_value  = sprintf("%.3f", tt$p.value))
}

t1_binary <- function(d, var, label) {
  ft  <- stats::fisher.test(table(d$race, d[[var]]))
  pct <- function(x) sprintf("%d (%.1f)", sum(x == 1, na.rm = TRUE),
                             100 * mean(x == 1, na.rm = TRUE))
  tibble(characteristic = label,
         overall  = pct(d[[var]]),
         nh_white = pct(d[[var]][d$race == "NH-White"]),
         nh_black = pct(d[[var]][d$race == "NH-Black"]),
         p_value  = sprintf("%.3f", ft$p.value))
}

t1_dat <- dat |>
  left_join(spec |> select(SampleID, all_of(species_vars)), by = "SampleID") |>
  mutate(late_stage = as.integer(stage == "Late"),
         type_ii    = as.integer(hist  == "Type II"))

table1 <- bind_rows(
  t1_continuous(t1_dat, "age",                     "Age at diagnosis, mean (SD), years"),
  t1_binary(    t1_dat, "late_stage",              "Late-stage disease"),
  t1_binary(    t1_dat, "type_ii",                 "Type II epithelial histology"),
  t1_continuous(t1_dat, "pss4_sum",                "PSS-4, mean (SD)"),
  t1_continuous(t1_dat, "shannon_diversity",       "Shannon diversity, mean (SD)"),
  t1_binary(    t1_dat, "lactobacillus_dominance", "Lactobacillus dominance"),
  t1_binary(    t1_dat, "crispatus_detected",      "L. crispatus detected"),
  t1_binary(    t1_dat, "iners_detected",          "L. iners detected"),
  t1_binary(    t1_dat, "gasseri_detected",        "L. gasseri detected"),
  t1_binary(    t1_dat, "jensenii_detected",       "L. jensenii detected")
)

cat("N overall:", nrow(t1_dat),
    "| NH-White:", sum(t1_dat$race == "NH-White"),
    "| NH-Black:", sum(t1_dat$race == "NH-Black"), "\n")
cat("PSS-4 range:", min(dat$pss4_sum), "-", max(dat$pss4_sum),
    "| participants scoring 0:", sum(dat$pss4_sum == 0),
    sprintf("(%.1f%%)", 100 * mean(dat$pss4_sum == 0)), "\n\n")
table1
```

# Species detection {#species}

**Question.** Is perceived stress associated with detection of each of the four
predominant vaginal *Lactobacillus* species?

**Model.** Firth penalized logistic regression adjusted for race and age.
Detection is binary; event counts are small (6–14) and one species is detected
in only one racial group, so penalization keeps estimates finite. Confidence
intervals are profile penalized-likelihood intervals. Only race and age are
included because additional covariates cannot be supported by 6–14 events. All
four species are fit in one loop with one formula so the four tests share a
specification.

**Multiple testing.** Benjamini–Hochberg correction across these four P values.

```{r species-primary}
species_results <- map_dfr(species_vars, function(v) {
  model <- logistf(as.formula(paste(v, "~ pss4_z + race + age")), data = spec)
  extract_firth_term(model, term = "pss4_z",
                     outcome    = unname(species_labels[v]),
                     adjustment = "Race and age", statistic = "OR") |>
    mutate(events = sum(spec[[v]] == 1, na.rm = TRUE))
}) |>
  mutate(fdr_q       = p.adjust(p_value, method = "BH"),
         estimate_ci = format_result(estimate, conf_low, conf_high)) |>
  select(outcome, statistic, estimate, conf_low, conf_high,
         estimate_ci, p_value, fdr_q, events, adjustment)

species_results
```

---

# Community and genus measures {#comparators}

Each is a different construct and is reported once with an unadjusted P value.
All three models are adjusted for race, age, stage, and histologic subtype.

## Shannon diversity

Linear regression; the outcome is continuous. Shannon diversity is calculated at
the amplicon sequence variant level.

```{r shannon}
m_shannon <- lm(shannon_diversity ~ pss4_z + race + age + stage + hist, data = dat)

shannon_result <- extract_lm_term(
  m_shannon, term = "pss4_z", outcome = "Shannon diversity",
  adjustment = "Race, age, stage, and histologic subtype", statistic = "Beta")
shannon_result
```

## *Lactobacillus* dominance

Dominance is supplied as an indicator of genus-level *Lactobacillus* relative
abundance of at least 50% (29 of 123 participants). Firth penalized logistic regression is used for all
binary outcomes so that a single estimator is applied throughout.

```{r dominance}
m_dom <- logistf(lactobacillus_dominance ~ pss4_z + race + age + stage + hist,
                 data = dat)

dominance_result <- extract_firth_term(
  m_dom, term = "pss4_z", outcome = "Lactobacillus dominance",
  adjustment = "Race, age, stage, and histologic subtype", statistic = "OR")
dominance_result
```

## *Lactobacillus*-dominated topic

Topics come from the latent Dirichlet allocation fit in the parent ORCHiD
analysis (seven topics). Topic numbering is not stable across fits, so the
*Lactobacillus*-dominated topic is identified as the topic with the highest mean
membership proportion (gamma) among *Lactobacillus*-dominant samples rather than
by a hard-coded number.

Membership is a proportion bounded by 0 and 1, so it is modeled with beta
regression and a logit link; the coefficient is exponentiated and is the ratio
of the odds μ/(1−μ) of expected membership per 1-SD increase in PSS-4. Beta
regression requires values strictly inside (0, 1); the chunk stops if any
membership proportion is exactly 0 or 1.

```{r topic}
topic_obj <- readr::read_rds(read_input("topic_model_results.rds"))

gamma_wide <- topic_obj$gamma |>
  mutate(topic_label = paste0("Topic", topic)) |>
  select(document, topic_label, gamma) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = topic_label, values_from = gamma) |>
  rename(SampleID = document)

topic_cols <- grep("^Topic", names(gamma_wide), value = TRUE)

beta_dat <- dat |> inner_join(gamma_wide, by = "SampleID")
stopifnot(nrow(beta_dat) == nrow(dat))

mean_gamma <- colMeans(beta_dat |> filter(lactobacillus_dominance == 1) |>
                         select(all_of(topic_cols)), na.rm = TRUE)
cat("Mean membership per topic among Lactobacillus-dominant samples:\n")
print(round(mean_gamma, 3))

lacto_topic <- names(mean_gamma)[which.max(mean_gamma)]
cat("\nLactobacillus-dominated topic:", lacto_topic, "\n")

rng <- range(beta_dat[[lacto_topic]])
cat("Membership range:", signif(rng, 3), "\n")
if (rng[1] <= 0 || rng[2] >= 1) {
  stop("Topic membership includes exact 0 or 1; beta regression requires a ",
       "transformation that is not part of the reported analysis.")
}

beta_dat$topic_y <- beta_dat[[lacto_topic]]
m_topic <- betareg(topic_y ~ pss4_z + race + age + stage + hist,
                   data = beta_dat, link = "logit")

topic_ci <- confint(m_topic)["pss4_z", ]
topic_result <- tibble(
  outcome    = "Lactobacillus-dominated topic membership",
  statistic  = "exp(Beta)",
  estimate   = exp(coef(m_topic)[["pss4_z"]]),
  conf_low   = exp(topic_ci[[1]]),
  conf_high  = exp(topic_ci[[2]]),
  p_value    = summary(m_topic)$coefficients$mean["pss4_z", "Pr(>|z|)"],
  adjustment = "Race, age, stage, and histologic subtype"
)
topic_result
```

# Table 2 and Figure 1 {#table2}

```{r table2}
comparator_results <- bind_rows(shannon_result, dominance_result, topic_result) |>
  mutate(estimate_ci = format_result(estimate, conf_low, conf_high)) |>
  select(outcome, statistic, estimate, conf_low, conf_high,
         estimate_ci, p_value, adjustment)

table2 <- bind_rows(
  species_results |> select(outcome, events, statistic, estimate, conf_low,
                            conf_high, p_value, fdr_q, adjustment),
  comparator_results |>
    left_join(analysis_counts |> select(outcome, events) |>
                mutate(outcome = recode(outcome,
                  "Lactobacillus dominance (>=50%)" = "Lactobacillus dominance")),
              by = "outcome") |>
    mutate(fdr_q = NA_real_) |>
    select(outcome, events, statistic, estimate, conf_low, conf_high,
           p_value, fdr_q, adjustment)
)
table2
```

**Figure 1.** Panel a: odds ratios (the topic estimate is exp[β]) on a log scale
for species detection, dominance, and topic membership, with event counts and q
values. Panel b: the Shannon diversity coefficient on its own linear scale,
because it is a different quantity.

```{r figure1, fig.width=9, fig.height=6.5}
col_blue <- "#2166A8"; col_red <- "#BF4A14"
minus <- function(x) gsub("-", "\u2212", x, fixed = TRUE)

fig1_a_dat <- table2 |>
  filter(outcome != "Shannon diversity") |>
  mutate(label  = ifelse(is.na(events), outcome, paste0(outcome, " (", events, ")")),
         label  = fct_rev(fct_inorder(label)),
         est_ci = minus(sprintf("%.2f (%.2f\u2013%.2f)", estimate, conf_low, conf_high)),
         q_txt  = ifelse(is.na(fdr_q), "", sprintf("%.3f", fdr_q)))

fig1_a <- ggplot(fig1_a_dat, aes(x = estimate, y = label)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
  geom_errorbar(aes(xmin = conf_low, xmax = conf_high), orientation = "y",
                width = 0.25, colour = col_blue, linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_point(size = 3.2, shape = 16, colour = col_blue) +
  geom_text(aes(x = 6, label = est_ci), hjust = 0, size = 3.4) +
  geom_text(aes(x = 17, label = q_txt), hjust = 0, size = 3.4) +
  annotate("text", x = 6,  y = nrow(fig1_a_dat) + 0.8, label = "Estimate (95% CI)",
           hjust = 0, size = 3.6) +
  annotate("text", x = 17, y = nrow(fig1_a_dat) + 0.8, label = "q", hjust = 0, size = 3.6) +
  scale_x_log10(breaks = c(0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 4)) +
  coord_cartesian(clip = "off", xlim = c(0.2, 4), ylim = c(0.6, nrow(fig1_a_dat) + 0.4)) +
  labs(x = "OR (topic: exp[\u03b2]) per 1-SD increase in PSS-4", y = NULL) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 11) +
  theme(axis.line.y = element_blank(), axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
        plot.margin = margin(14, 150, 4, 4))

fig1_b_dat <- table2 |>
  filter(outcome == "Shannon diversity") |>
  mutate(est_ci = minus(sprintf("%.2f (%.2f to %.2f)", estimate, conf_low, conf_high)))

fig1_b <- ggplot(fig1_b_dat, aes(x = estimate, y = outcome)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
  geom_errorbar(aes(xmin = conf_low, xmax = conf_high), orientation = "y",
                width = 0.25, colour = col_blue, linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_point(size = 3.2, shape = 16, colour = col_blue) +
  geom_text(aes(x = 0.75, label = est_ci), hjust = 0, size = 3.4) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(-0.6, 0, 0.6)) +
  coord_cartesian(clip = "off", xlim = c(-0.6, 0.6)) +
  labs(x = "\u03b2 per 1-SD increase in PSS-4", y = NULL) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 11) +
  theme(axis.line.y = element_blank(), axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
        plot.margin = margin(4, 150, 4, 4))

figure1 <- fig1_a / fig1_b + plot_layout(heights = c(6, 1.4)) +
  plot_annotation(tag_levels = "a")
figure1
```

---

# Race interaction and stratified models {#race}

**Question.** Does the PSS-4 association with Shannon diversity or *Lactobacillus*
dominance differ between NH-Black (n = 20) and NH-White (n = 103) participants?

Two different analyses are run for the same two outcomes:

1. **Interaction models** (`pss4_z * race + age`) formally test whether the PSS-4
   slope differs between racial groups. The interaction coefficient is the
   NH-Black minus NH-White difference in slopes (for dominance, exponentiated:
   the ratio of the two groups' odds ratios).
2. **Stratified models** (`pss4_z + age`, fit separately within each group)
   describe the association within each group. They do **not** test whether the
   groups differ.

Models are adjusted for age only, to preserve degrees of freedom in the
20-participant stratum. Interaction and stratified models are not fit for
species-level outcomes (4 *L. iners* detections among NH-Black participants) or
for topic membership.

```{r race-interaction}
shannon_int_result <- extract_lm_term(
  lm(shannon_diversity ~ pss4_z * race + age, data = dat),
  term = "pss4_z:raceNH-Black", outcome = "Shannon diversity",
  adjustment = "Age", statistic = "Interaction beta")

dominance_int_result <- extract_firth_term(
  logistf(lactobacillus_dominance ~ pss4_z * race + age, data = dat),
  term = "pss4_z:raceNH-Black", outcome = "Lactobacillus dominance",
  adjustment = "Age", statistic = "Interaction OR")

interaction_results <- bind_rows(shannon_int_result, dominance_int_result) |>
  mutate(estimate_ci = format_result(estimate, conf_low, conf_high, digits = 3))
interaction_results
```

```{r race-stratified}
shannon_stratified <- dat |>
  group_split(race) |>
  set_names(levels(dat$race)) |>
  map_dfr(function(df) {
    broom::tidy(lm(shannon_diversity ~ pss4_z + age, data = df), conf.int = TRUE) |>
      filter(term == "pss4_z") |>
      transmute(statistic = "Beta", estimate,
                conf_low = conf.low, conf_high = conf.high, p_value = p.value)
  }, .id = "race") |>
  mutate(outcome = "Shannon diversity", .after = race)

dominance_stratified <- dat |>
  group_split(race) |>
  set_names(levels(dat$race)) |>
  map_dfr(function(df) {
    extract_firth_term(logistf(lactobacillus_dominance ~ pss4_z + age, data = df),
                       "pss4_z", "Lactobacillus dominance", "Age", "OR") |>
      select(statistic, estimate, conf_low, conf_high, p_value)
  }, .id = "race") |>
  mutate(outcome = "Lactobacillus dominance", .after = race)

stratified_results <- bind_rows(shannon_stratified, dominance_stratified) |>
  mutate(n = ifelse(race == "NH-White", sum(dat$race == "NH-White"),
                    sum(dat$race == "NH-Black")), .after = race,
         estimate_ci = format_result(estimate, conf_low, conf_high))
stratified_results
```

**Figure 2.** Race-stratified estimates, with the interaction P value from the
interaction models above. Circles are NH-White participants and squares are
NH-Black participants. Panel a: Shannon diversity, linear scale (null = 0).
Panel b: *Lactobacillus* dominance, odds ratio on a log scale (null = 1).

```{r figure2, fig.width=10, fig.height=5}
race_labels <- c("NH-White" = paste0("Non-Hispanic White (n=", sum(dat$race == "NH-White"), ")"),
                 "NH-Black" = paste0("Non-Hispanic Black (n=", sum(dat$race == "NH-Black"), ")"))

fig2_dat <- stratified_results |>
  mutate(race   = factor(race, levels = c("NH-Black", "NH-White")),
         est_ci = minus(ifelse(statistic == "Beta",
                               sprintf("%.2f (%.2f to %.2f)", estimate, conf_low, conf_high),
                               sprintf("%.2f (%.2f\u2013%.2f)", estimate, conf_low, conf_high))))

fig2_panel <- function(outcome_name, null_value, xlab, p_int, log_scale = FALSE,
                       limits = NULL, breaks = waiver()) {
  d <- fig2_dat |> filter(outcome == outcome_name)
  g <- ggplot(d, aes(x = estimate, y = race, colour = race, shape = race)) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = null_value, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
    geom_errorbar(aes(xmin = conf_low, xmax = conf_high), orientation = "y",
                  width = 0.12, linewidth = 0.6) +
    geom_point(size = 3.6) +
    geom_text(aes(x = if (log_scale) sqrt(prod(limits)) else mean(limits),
                  label = est_ci), vjust = -1.6, colour = "black", size = 3.5) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c("NH-White" = col_blue, "NH-Black" = col_red),
                        labels = race_labels, breaks = c("NH-White", "NH-Black")) +
    scale_shape_manual(values = c("NH-White" = 16, "NH-Black" = 15),   # circle, square
                       labels = race_labels, breaks = c("NH-White", "NH-Black")) +
    labs(x = paste0(xlab, "\nInteraction P=", sprintf("%.3f", p_int)), y = NULL,
         colour = NULL, shape = NULL) +
    theme_classic(base_size = 11) +
    theme(axis.line.y = element_blank(), axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
          axis.text.y = element_blank(), legend.position = "top")
  if (log_scale) g <- g + scale_x_log10(breaks = breaks)
  else g <- g + scale_x_continuous(breaks = breaks)
  g <- g + coord_cartesian(xlim = limits)   # zoom only; never drops CI endpoints
  g
}

fig2_a <- fig2_panel("Shannon diversity", 0, "\u03b2 per 1-SD increase in PSS-4",
                     interaction_results$p_value[1], limits = c(-1, 0.5),
                     breaks = c(-1, -0.5, 0, 0.5))
fig2_b <- fig2_panel("Lactobacillus dominance", 1, "Odds ratio per 1-SD increase in PSS-4",
                     interaction_results$p_value[2], log_scale = TRUE,
                     limits = c(0.5, 6), breaks = c(0.5, 1, 2, 4))

figure2 <- (fig2_a + fig2_b) +
  plot_layout(guides = "collect") + plot_annotation(tag_levels = "a") &
  theme(legend.position = "top")
figure2
```

```{r table3}
table3 <- bind_rows(
  interaction_results |> mutate(panel = "Interaction", race = NA_character_, n = NA_integer_),
  stratified_results  |> mutate(panel = "Race-stratified")
) |>
  select(panel, outcome, race, n, statistic, estimate, conf_low, conf_high, p_value)
table3
```

# Sensitivity analyses {#sensitivity}

None is corrected for multiple testing; each re-expresses a result reported
above. Together they form Supplementary Table S1.

## Expanded adjustment (species models)

Stage and histologic subtype are added to the four species models to check
whether the estimates depend on clinical covariates.

```{r sens-expanded}
species_expanded <- map_dfr(species_vars, function(v) {
  m <- logistf(as.formula(paste(v, "~ pss4_z + race + age + stage + hist")),
               data = spec)
  extract_firth_term(m, "pss4_z", unname(species_labels[v]),
                     "Race, age, stage, and histologic subtype", "OR")
}) |>
  mutate(estimate_ci = format_result(estimate, conf_low, conf_high))
species_expanded
```

## Omitting histologic subtype (Shannon diversity and dominance)

Histologic subtype creates the sparsest covariate cells; this checks whether the
Shannon diversity and dominance estimates depend on its inclusion.

```{r sens-nohist}
nohist_results <- bind_rows(
  extract_lm_term(lm(shannon_diversity ~ pss4_z + race + age + stage, data = dat),
                  "pss4_z", "Shannon diversity", "Race, age, and stage", "Beta"),
  extract_firth_term(logistf(lactobacillus_dominance ~ pss4_z + race + age + stage,
                             data = dat),
                     "pss4_z", "Lactobacillus dominance", "Race, age, and stage", "OR")
) |>
  mutate(estimate_ci = format_result(estimate, conf_low, conf_high))
nohist_results
```

## Dose–response among *L. iners* carriers

Spearman rank correlation between PSS-4 and *L. iners* relative abundance among
participants with *L. iners* detected. With 14 observations this is a direction
check only.

```{r sens-spearman}
iners_positive <- spec |> filter(iners_abundance > 0)
sp <- cor.test(iners_positive$pss4_sum, iners_positive$iners_abundance,
               method = "spearman", exact = FALSE)

spearman_result <- tibble(
  analysis = "PSS-4 and L. iners abundance among detected samples",
  n = nrow(iners_positive), rho = unname(sp$estimate), p_value = sp$p.value)
spearman_result
```

## Leave-one-out stability

The *L. iners* detection model is refit 123 times, omitting one participant each
time, to check that no single participant carries the association.

```{r sens-loo}
leave_one_out_firth <- function(data, formula, term = "pss4_z") {
  map_dfr(seq_len(nrow(data)), function(i) {
    fit <- tryCatch(logistf(formula, data = data[-i, , drop = FALSE]),
                    error = function(e) NULL)
    if (is.null(fit) || !term %in% names(coef(fit))) {
      return(tibble(removed_row = i, OR = NA_real_, ci_low = NA_real_))
    }
    idx <- match(term, names(coef(fit)))
    tibble(removed_row = i, OR = exp(coef(fit)[[term]]), ci_low = exp(fit$ci.lower[idx]))
  })
}

loo_iners <- leave_one_out_firth(spec, iners_detected ~ pss4_z + race + age)

loo_summary <- tibble(
  model = "L. iners detection", n_refits = nrow(loo_iners),
  or_min = min(loo_iners$OR, na.rm = TRUE), or_median = median(loo_iners$OR, na.rm = TRUE),
  or_max = max(loo_iners$OR, na.rm = TRUE),
  refits_ci_above1 = sum(loo_iners$ci_low > 1, na.rm = TRUE))
loo_summary
```

## Departure from linearity

For Shannon diversity, a linear PSS-4 term is compared with a natural cubic
spline with 3 degrees of freedom (`ns(pss4_sum, df = 3)`; knots are placed
automatically). For dominance, a quadratic PSS-4 term is tested using the
penalized likelihood-ratio P value. These are specification checks.

```{r sens-linearity}
m_lin    <- lm(shannon_diversity ~ pss4_sum + race + age + stage + hist, data = dat)
m_spline <- lm(shannon_diversity ~ ns(pss4_sum, df = 3) + race + age + stage + hist,
               data = dat)
lin_shannon <- anova(m_lin, m_spline)
lin_shannon

m_dom_quad <- logistf(
  lactobacillus_dominance ~ pss4_z + I(pss4_z^2) + race + age + stage + hist,
  data = dat)
quad_p <- m_dom_quad$prob[match("I(pss4_z^2)", names(coef(m_dom_quad)))]

linearity_results <- tibble(
  outcome   = c("Shannon diversity", "Lactobacillus dominance"),
  test      = c("3-df natural cubic spline vs linear (F test)",
                "Quadratic PSS-4 term (penalized likelihood ratio)"),
  statistic = c(lin_shannon$F[2], NA_real_),
  p_value   = c(lin_shannon$`Pr(>F)`[2], quad_p))
linearity_results
```

## Supplementary Table S1

```{r table-s1}
tableS1 <- bind_rows(
  species_expanded |>
    transmute(analysis = paste0("Expanded adjustment: ", outcome), n = nrow(spec),
              measure = "OR", estimate, conf_low, conf_high, p_value),
  nohist_results |>
    transmute(analysis = paste0("Omit histologic subtype: ", outcome), n = nrow(dat),
              measure = statistic, estimate, conf_low, conf_high, p_value),
  spearman_result |>
    transmute(analysis = analysis, n = n, measure = "rho", estimate = rho,
              conf_low = NA_real_, conf_high = NA_real_, p_value),
  loo_summary |>
    transmute(analysis = "Leave-one-out: L. iners detection (OR range)", n = n_refits,
              measure = "OR range", estimate = NA_real_, conf_low = or_min,
              conf_high = or_max, p_value = NA_real_),
  linearity_results |>
    transmute(analysis = paste0("Departure from linearity: ", outcome), n = nrow(dat),
              measure = ifelse(is.na(statistic), "-", "F"),
              estimate = statistic, conf_low = NA_real_, conf_high = NA_real_, p_value)
)
tableS1
```
